summary: Create a new telegram-config governed-state surface defining the Telegram bot's runtime parameters: token path, allowed user IDs, webhook settings, and rate limits.
rationale: Xavier wants to run an AI_Cicibot on Telegram. For Cici to operate safely as a Telegram bot, the runtime parameters (bot token env var name, allowed Telegram user IDs, webhook URL, message rate limits) must be governed — not hardcoded in the bot runtime. This surface gives the bot code a canonical, version-controlled source of truth for how the Telegram bridge behaves, and prevents accidental changes to security-critical settings (allowed user list) without an explicit proposal.
evidence_refs: CLAUDE.md — 'What This Repo Is' and governed-state doctrine
config/authority-map.json — canonical write class requires proposal for new surfaces
proposed_diff_summary: Create users/cici/governed-state/telegram-config/ directory with config.json containing: env_var_names (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS), allowed_user_ids placeholder (Xavier fills at runtime), webhook_mode (polling for local dev, webhook for production), rate_limit_per_user_per_minute: 20, max_message_length: 4000. Add surface entry to surface-map.json with status 'active'.
